newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIAN SHARES INCH UP IN MORE ACTIVE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIAN SHARES INCH UP IN MORE ACTIVE TRADE.

text.p: Latvian shares rose slightly in more active trade on Wednesday and dealers said that further gains were on the horizon as low prices lure investors back to the struggling market.
Turnover more than doubled to 108,000 lats from 51,000 lats and the bourse index edged up by 0.54 percent to 386.04. The Rietumu index climbed 0.5 percent to 150.49.
Three of the six official list stocks gained, two eased and one held steady.
Unibanka led the way, rising to 3.37 lats from 3.33 lats as 36,700 lats worth of its shares changed hands.
Dealers said the bank, which recently saw one million of its shares auctioned off by the state, has good potential to rise and could help boost the rest of the market.
Dealers remain hopeful that bargain prices will bring buyers to the bourse but admit that bigger, better companies need to be listed before the market will really take off.
Elsewhere on the official list, the Riga Shipyard inched up to 1.30 lats from 1.29 lats in trade of 5,100 lats while the Kaija Fish cannery rose to 2.12 lats from 2.10 lats.
Staburadze Confectionery was stable at 2.71 lats in trade of 33,500 lats.
On the secondary list, Jekabpils Sugar eased 2.9 percent to 66 santimes in trade of 13,200 lats.
The company's interim profit results far exceeded the market's expectations but dealers say that the seasonal nature of the industry casts doubt on its ability to perform as well in the second half.
